reports.title: APP vs. U: This Game Isn't Zero-Sum
reports.headline: MS argues APP and U can both grow in mobile app ads as better targeting expands conversions, while APP remains OW despite PT cut to $450 from $650.
reports.summary: MS pushes back on investor concern that U's Vector success must pressure APP, arguing the ~$80bn mobile app ad market and ~1% conversion rates leave room for both networks to grow by improving targeting and ROAS. Vector's q/q growth trajectory compares favorably to APP ad rev growth after AXON 2.0 launch, suggesting U is early in a similar optimization cycle.
Rising CPMs are framed as stronger advertiser demand and improving ROAS, not necessarily destructive competition between APP and U.

reports.title: WRG Health Care Understanding 340B Regulatory and Legislative Policy Efforts
reports.headline: 340B reform momentum rising, but NT action likely administrative not legislative
reports.summary: TD Cowen sees bipartisan 340B reform momentum building in DC, but expects the most likely NT changes to come from admin action: HRSA’s Jan 2027 rebate-model pilot and CMS’s CY27 OPPS proposal cutting 340B Medicare drug reimbursement to ASP -33.4%, likely finalized in Nov 2026. Major legislation is viewed as unlikely in the next 24 mos despite bipartisan House/Senate drafting, but feasible over 3-5 yrs, likely as part of a broader HC package that offsets pressure on non-profit hospitals and possibly pharma tailwinds.
important_observations: Admin reform is the key NT catalyst, with CMS likely to finalize ASP -33.4% for 340B-acquired drugs in early Nov 2026.
OPPS change is framed as a lift for for-profit hospitals while pressuring non-profit hospitals’ 340B economics and influencing contract-pharmacy behavior.
HRSA rebate pilot starts Jan 1, 2027 and applies only to IRA-negotiated drugs, limiting breadth despite signaling a broader policy direction.

Bipartisan SUSTAIN/SECURE bills align on clearinghouse-based duplicate-discount controls, tighter patient definitions, more transparency, audits/enforcement, and PBM/payer nondiscrimination protections.
Legislative reform is unlikely in the next 24 mos due to lack of HC vehicles and concern about compounding non-profit hospital headwinds.
new_data: CMS CY27 OPPS proposal would cut Medicare reimbursement for 340B-acquired drugs from ASP +6% to ASP -33.4%.
The ASP -33.4% level is based on survey findings that 340B hospitals acquire drugs at roughly 33.4% below ASP.
HRSA pilot expected to go live Jan 1, 2027 for 2026 and 2027 IRA-negotiated drugs.
Pilot-covered IRA drugs represented 24% of total drug sales and 21% of mail-channel sales in 2025.
Senate SUSTAIN introduced in Aug 2026; House SECURE introduced in Jul 2026; Cassidy discussion draft released in Jun 2026.
evidence_quality: Policy/regulatory sourcing: primary government proposals and pilot details drive the NT catalyst view; high weight for timing and mechanics.
Legislative analysis: analyst inference from bill text, bipartisan sponsorship, stakeholder positions, and expected congressional vehicles; moderate weight.
Market/industry data: drug-sales exposure figures help size HRSA pilot impact; useful but narrow to affected drug cohorts.
Stakeholder read-through: pharma generally supportive, non-profit hospitals opposed, contract pharmacies lobbying; directional and partly inference-based.
risks_or_watch_items: CMS could alter or delay final OPPS policy despite analyst expectation it is finalized as proposed.
Legal challenges remain a risk given prior 340B reimbursement policy was struck down by SCOTUS before CMS reworked its evidentiary basis.
Future Dem control after 2028 could change reform shape, likely requiring offsets for non-profit hospitals and potentially pharma.
Loss of a key individual Senate champion may reduce odds of legislative passage.
Contract-pharmacy lobbying could reshape final legislative provisions.
